Adaptive thinking.d: How current Claude models reason: for each request the model decides whether to think before answering and how much. You steer it with an effort level rather than a fixed thinking budget.

Chain of thought.d: Step-by-step reasoning a model writes out before its final answer. The written steps give it more computation and somewhere to keep intermediate results.

Test-time compute.d: Extra computation spent while a model answers (mainly thinking tokens), as opposed to computation spent training it. Also called inference-time compute.

Context rot.d: Anthropic's name for the drop in accuracy and recall as the amount of text in a model's context window grows. The reason to curate context rather than fill it.

Lost in the middle.d: The finding (Liu et al., 2023) that language models use information at the start and end of a long input more reliably than information in the middle.

Auto memory.d: Notes Claude Code writes for itself about a project, stored on your machine and loaded into the context at the start of each session. On by default; managed with /memory.

Prompt caching.d: An API feature that stores the processed beginning of a prompt for a short time so repeated requests reuse it more cheaply and quickly. Cached tokens still count toward the context window.

Vision encoder.d: The part of a multimodal model that turns an image (cut into small patches) into vectors the language model can read alongside text.

Visual token.d: Anthropic's term for one 28x28-pixel patch of an image as Claude processes it. An image costs roughly (width/28) x (height/28) visual tokens.

Speech-to-text.d: Turning spoken audio into written text, also called transcription or automatic speech recognition. Often the first step before a language model works on speech.

Diffusion model.d: The kind of model behind most image and video generators: it starts from random noise and removes it step by step, guided by a text description, until an image appears.
